brute_force.name: Permutation Generation & Lexicographical Ordering
brute_force.technique: Generate all unique permutations recursively or iteratively, sort them in lexicographical order, locate the current permutation, and pick the subsequent permutation (wrapping around to the first if currently at the last).
brute_force.teaches: Clarifies the exact mathematical definition of lexicographical ordering and next permutation, while exposing why factorial exponential growth makes full generation completely unfeasible and space-prohibitive.

optimal.name: Right-to-Left Pivot Scan, Successor Swap & Suffix Reversal
optimal.technique: 1) Scan right-to-left for the first dip i where nums[i] < nums[i+1]. 2) Scan right-to-left for the first value nums[j] > nums[i]. 3) Swap nums[i] and nums[j]. 4) Reverse the non-increasing suffix nums[i+1..n-1] in-place with two pointers.
optimal.teaches: Demonstrates why a non-increasing suffix represents a local maximum arrangement that cannot be increased further, why the rightmost descent is the minimal pivot point to modify, and how reversing an already-reversed suffix yields the minimal lexicographical sequence without comparison sorting.

decision_reasoning.D1_brute_teaches_why: Brute force establishes the exact concept of lexicographical order and the immediate-successor requirement on a small testcase [1, 2, 3], while highlighting the catastrophic factorial O(N!) space/time failure.
decision_reasoning.D2_better_distinct: The single-pass linear approach O(N) time and O(1) space exploits the structural property of non-increasing suffixes directly in-place.
decision_reasoning.D3_dp_progression: N/A — In-place array manipulation & lexicographical sequence mathematics.
decision_reasoning.D4_data_structure_problem: In-place array two-pointer reversal and right-to-left pivot indexing.
decision_reasoning.D5_fewer_is_better: Two distinct approaches (Brute Force Generation -> Optimal Right-to-Left Scan & Reverse) provide the standard 10-scene pedagogical progression.
